ours.name: Ragged Edge
ours.approach: Same trailhead and trail as True Grit: Sunrise Mine Trail #707 from the Sunrise Mine Trailhead on the Mountain Loop Highway, through second-growth forest and an early creek crossing of the South Fork Stillaguamish (log crossing, harder in high runoff), up through Wirtz Basin and out onto open, cairned talus, then through Headlee Pass (~4,720 ft, 2.7 mi, loose rock/rockfall exposure in the narrow couloir) and down to Vesper Creek and Vesper Lake (Lake Elan, ~5,000 ft, ~3.5 mi/~2,700 ft gain) — the last dependable water. From the lake the maintained trail fades; cross the outlet and follow an obvious talus ridgeline up to the saddle between Vesper and Wolf Peak, the small summit just northeast
ours.descent: No rappels are required — Ragged Edge tops out at or very near Vesper's summit, and the standard exit is a walk-off down the peak's east side/East Ridge back toward the Vesper-Wolf saddle, then down to Vesper Lake and out the Sunrise Mine Trail. fktText: Description A classic Cascades scramble with big payoff for relatively little technical skill required. From the Sunrise Mine Trail, cross Vesper Creek instead of heading toward Vesper Lake. A bootpath climbs steeply through heather, cedar, and rocky slopes before breaking onto granite slabs. From here, it’s straightforward off-trail scrambling: mostly low-angle rock, with light hands-on moves and easy routefinding. Stay on the central rib to avoid gullies (left) or exposure (right). The airy summit delivers commanding views of Del Campo, Gothic, Sperry, Big Four, and the Vesper Glacier dropping to Copper Lake. ours.name: Southeast Ridge (Crater Lake Approach)
ours.approach: From Twisp, take Highway 20 south ~2 miles to WA-153, then south on WA-153 to County Rd 1029 (Gold Creek Loop), continuing onto County Rd 1034 (Gold Creek Road), which becomes Forest Road 4340 after about 6 miles. Turn onto FR 4340-300 (Crater Creek Road) and follow it about 4.6 miles to the Crater Creek Trailhead (~4,750 ft; day-use fee $5, or $30/yr — Northwest Forest Pass/interagency passes accepted). Hike the Crater Creek/Crater Lakes Trail about 3.9 miles one-way, gaining roughly 2,100 ft, to Lower Crater Lake (about 6,840 ft), then continue off-trail up the southeast ridge to the ~8,000 ft col and on to the summit.
ours.descent: From the summit, downclimb the boulder scramble back to the ~8,000 ft col, then descend into the Crater Lake basin. In the one documented winter ascent, the party skied this descent back to a camp at Crater Lake before skiing/hiking out the following day via the unplowed Crater Creek Road.

fktText: Description Route submitted by Ryan Stoddard : This route is in the Sawtooth sub-range of WA's Cascades. The only requirements are to start and end at Crater Creek TH and summit the five top 100 "Bulger" list peaks along the way: Switchback, Bigelow, Martin, Raven Ridge, Hoodoo. Note that the True summit of Raven Ridge is a little east of the ridge line (this one: https://peakbagger.com/peak.aspx?pid=28897 ) not Libby Peak. ours.name: True Grit
ours.approach: Start at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead (Sunrise Mine Trail #707) off the Mountain Loop Highway near Big Four/Barlow Pass. The trail begins in second-growth forest and almost immediately crosses the South Fork Stillaguamish via a log crossing that can be a genuine obstacle during high runoff (early season/after rain). From there the trail climbs steadily through Wirtz Basin, breaks out of the trees into open talus and boulder fields marked by cairns, and reaches Headlee Pass at roughly 4,720 ft and 2.7 miles in — a narrow, rocky notch/couloir with loose rock underfoot where rockfall from parties above is a real hazard. ours.name: Standard Route (Headlee Pass)
ours.approach: From the Sunrise Mine trailhead, Trail 707 crosses several streams in the first mile, including the main South Fork Stillaguamish, which has no bridge and can be a serious obstacle when runoff is high. The trail then climbs through forest and an open talus basin before tightening into steep, narrow switchbacks up the couloir to Headlee Pass, about 2.7 miles from the trailhead. From the pass, the trail traverses the south flank of Sperry Peak into the upper Vesper Creek basin, where the route leaves the lake trail at the creek crossing.
ours.descent: Descend the same way. Take care to find the central rib again on the slabs, since the gullies to the descender's right lead into steeper ground, and go slowly down the loose Headlee Pass couloir.
